- Scheme and requirements draft is on Drive: `PFF_endpoint/athlete_profiles/scheme_requirements_draft.md`. It uses `PP_Recruiting / 000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` as the position-requirement source, and reads Baylor's 2024 and 2025 offense from PFF video plays (shotgun about 85%, one personnel grouping most of the time).
- Step 1 split test (`scripts/split_stability.py`, output `data/split_stability.csv`): shotgun and down-and-distance splits do not clear the reliability rule. OL pressure is 0.59 split-half in shotgun, same as all rows. Passing-down year-to-year has too few pairs.
- Scheme read for all four seasons (`scripts/scheme_read.py`, outputs `data/scheme_read_<season>.csv`, counts and shares only): shotgun 76% (2023), 83%, 86%, 86% (2026 partial). Single personnel grouping 47% in 2023, then 73% to 82%. Play counts for 2024 and 2025 match the earlier database read.
- Decisions on 2026-10-23: use GRD SCALE thresholds as written; accept time-to-pressure as the OL pressure proxy; pull 2023 and 2026 video plays (done, in the PFF_Data_Project data folder, gitignored).
- Draft in Drive: `scheme_requirements_draft.md` updated in place, with the OC background and scheme lineage section (Holgorsen lineage is inference). Copy kept as `scheme_requirements_draft_v1.md`.

## Next

1. **Checkpoint rebuilds: 2026-12-02 (regular season done) and 2026-12-30 (before the January portal window).** The weekly PFF job writes a `pff-checkpoint: DUE` line to `.errors.log` that week, so the session-start block shows it. The agent in that session does this, unasked:
   - Make the venv once: `uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt`. Run every script below as `.venv/bin/python scripts/<name>.py` from the repo root.
   - Not on Wednesday 10:20 to about 11:00: the weekly job locks the DB. Check: `pgrep -f "run_pipeline.py --catch-up"` prints nothing.
   - `.venv/bin/python scripts/pff_weeks.py` shows the weeks the next pull will use (from the DB) and their default test weeks. On 12-30 the 2 latest weeks are 14-15 (few games): set `PFF_TEST_WEEKS` by hand, for example `12,13`.
   - Pulls (about 2 h in all; run in Terminal under `caffeinate -i -s`, per the long-jobs rule; all 7 in one sitting, because they share `data/weeks_2026.json`), each with `PFF_SEASON=2026`: `pull_fbs.py`, `pull_fbs_v3.py`, `pull_defense.py`, `pull_oline.py`, `pull_positions.py`, `pull_wr.py`, `pull_wr_targets.py`.
   - Each pull records its weeks and failures in `data/weeks_2026.json` when it finishes. The models stop unless all 7 pulls finished with 0 failures and the same weeks; re-run the pull it names.
   - Models: `qb_v4.py`, `ol_v2.py`, `pos_model.py`, `wr_model.py`, then `driver.py` (it reads the ol_v2 and pos outputs).
   - Profiles and splits: `qb_full_player_game.py`, then `PFF_QB_CSV=data/qb_full_player_game.csv .venv/bin/python scripts/metric_stability.py` (without `PFF_QB_CSV` the QB rows drop out, and so do the QB profiles), `athlete_profile.py`, `split_stability.py`. Fixed 2026-10-31 after the Codex review (profiles counted OL, WR and QB snaps twice; split stability dropped zero-target splits and skipped the OL season minimum), so the Drive copies of these outputs and the split numbers in Current state predate the fix.
   - Write the reports to Drive `PFF_endpoint/reports/<position>/`, dated, beside the old ones. Clear the DUE line from `.errors.log` when done.
2. Optional: a dated launchd job for the checkpoint pulls (the code is on main now). Not needed for 12-02: the DUE line in `.errors.log` triggers the rebuild.
3. Decide whether to build WR receptions and yards-after-catch features, now that a receiver id is confirmed.
4. Decide whether to re-pull the charting feed with the video-play receiver field, after its id type is checked.
5. Later: point the position scripts at the PFF DB instead of their own API pulls (the repo rule says not to duplicate the pipeline).
6. Add opponent strength to WR, LB, DB and RB, as done for QB (decision audit 2026-10-31).

## Open questions

- ANSWERED 2026-10-31: Outcome for the next round: keep PFF grade per game, or switch to EPA or a coach-rated outcome? Keep PFF grade per game (not EPA, not coach-rated).
- Receiver id in the video plays feed (`pass_receiver_target`): not matched to roster ids yet. Id type unknown.
- ANSWERED 2026-10-31: Add opponent strength to WR, LB, DB and RB (done for QB only)? Yes, all four, as done for QB.
- ANSWERED 2026-10-31: Which GRD SCALE traits can be tested from PFF, and whether to re-weight the eight factors? Use as written; no re-weighting of the eight factors.
- ANSWERED 2026-10-31: Pressure proxy (`time_to_pressure` set) is not the PFF pressure grade: accept it or find a true flag? Accept `time_to_pressure` as the proxy (as decided 10-23); line closed.

## Gotchas

- The pull scripts open the PFF DB read-only to pick the 2026 weeks. That fails while the weekly job (Wed 10:20, a few minutes) holds the write lock; set `PFF_PULL_WEEKS` (for example `1-13`) to skip the DB. The pulls record the weeks in `data/weeks_2026.json`; the models read only that file, never the DB. `PFF_CURRENT_WEEKS` on a model run picks a subset of the pulled weeks (to reproduce an older run); it cannot add weeks.
- Weeks 0 and 6 were left out of the original week set. The reason was not recorded. Week 6 is now in for 2026.
- Receiver link: premium passing `target_player_id` matches a WR grade row in the same game for only about 48% to 56% of target ids. The rest are TEs, RBs or others.
- Field roles are unverified against the PFF docs: `tackler_player_id`, `pass_rush` `player_id`, `runner_player_id`, `target_player_id`, and the premium `all_blocking` and `pressure` ids.
- The 2023 WR pull had 2 failed game calls (426 of 428 read). Not re-pulled.
- Scratch venv and probe scripts live outside the repo (in the session scratchpad). Only pull and model scripts are committed.
- Git: an automatic session-end commit (not from the user) added two scripts earlier. Its message is generic.

1. **Checkpoint rebuilds: 2026-12-02 (regular season done) and 2026-12-30 (before the January portal window).** The weekly PFF job writes a `pff-checkpoint: DUE` line to `.errors.log` that week, so the session-start block shows it. The agent in that session does this, unasked:

   - Not on Wednesday 10:20 to about 11:00: the weekly job locks the DB. Check: `pgrep -f "run_pipeline.py --catch-up"` prints nothing.
   - `.venv/bin/python scripts/pff_weeks.py` shows the weeks the next pull will use (from the DB) and their default test weeks. On 12-30 the 2 latest weeks are 14-15 (few games): set `PFF_TEST_WEEKS` by hand, for example `12,13`.

Fixed 2026-10-31 after the Codex review (profiles counted OL, WR and QB snaps twice; split stability dropped zero-target splits and skipped the OL season minimum), so the Drive copies of these outputs and the split numbers in Current state predate the fix.

# PFF_Position_Reports

## Purpose

- Explore all PFF advanced-metric endpoints and record what each one returns.
- Build position-group reports, modeled on the existing O-line and QB advanced reports. Order: O-line, then QB, then WR, RB, LB, DB.
- Later: a performance-driver analysis on a Power Four cross-section, for end-of-season roster evaluation and portal targets.
- Outcome variable is not decided yet. Default: PFF grade per game.

## Rules

- The PFF data pipeline lives in `erash11/PFF_Data_Project`. This repo reads from it. Never duplicate that pipeline here.
- Never commit `.env` files, API keys, bearer tokens, or raw PFF data. Keep extracts out of git, in the gitignored `data/` folder.
- Reports and outputs go to the Google Drive `PFF_endpoint` folder, not to this repo.
- Do not join PFF data to GPS or force-plate datasets. If a master table is needed, build a standalone master athlete table.
- Writing: plain and direct. No em dashes.

## Session routine

1. At start: `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md`.
2. At end: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
3. Never leave uncommitted work.
